name: Daniel Carroll
bio: A Delegate and a Representative from Maryland; born in Upper Marlboro, Prince George's County, Md., July 22, 1730; educated at the Jesuit School at Bohemia Manor, Md., and at St. Omer's College, France; returned to Maryland in 1748; member of the Md. state executive council, 1778-1781; Delegate to the Second Continental Congress, 1781; signed the Articles of Confederation; Delegate to the Confederation Congress, 1781-1783; delegate to the Federal Constitutional Convention in 1787; signed the U.S. Constitution; member of the Maryland state senate, 1781-1789 and served as president, 1786-1787; elected as a Pro-Administration candidate to the First Congress (March 4, 1789-March 3, 1791); took an active part in fixing the seat of government for the United States; appointed on March 4, 1791, as one of the commissioners to locate the District of Columbia and the Federal City and served until July 25, 1795, when he resigned; engaged in agricultural pursuits, his farm being the site of the present city of Washington; died at Rock Creek (Forest Glen), near Washington, D.C., May 7, 1796.
